## CIEC-1(b)

> Please provide Mr. Velez's estimate of the number of existing heat pump customers who would be automatically enrolled in Rate HP, and identify the source of that estimate [@ciec_Docket260510First_2026].

**Response.** Between **7,928** and **109,127** customers, or 0.65% to 9% of the 1,212,521 residential customers Eversource filed for the Rate Year [@clp_Docket260510Exhibit_2026g].

The direct testimony recommends that the Company auto-enroll every known residential customer who has already installed a heat pump. The customers it treats as readily identifiable are those who previously received a heat pump incentive through EnergizeCT or another state or utility program [@velez_Docket260510Direct_2026, p. 93, lines 7–12]. Customers who installed a heat pump outside those programs would be identified by attestation [@velez_Docket260510Direct_2026, p. 96, lines 9–11].

- **7,928** is the floor. It is the 4,400 customers the Company reports have received rebates since 2023 for a heat pump that fully displaced the prior heating system,[^clf-sc-003] plus the 3,528 residential customers its sales forecast expects to install a heat pump through the Conservation and Load Management program in 2026.[^clf-sc-001] Those 2026 installations would already be in place when Rate HP takes effect. The Company states that the rebate count is not every heat pump customer and that it does not track heating source.
- **109,127** is the ceiling, and it is the eligible group. It applies the share of Eversource households that heat primarily with a heat pump, 9% in the 2024 Connecticut Residential Appliance Saturation Survey, to the Rate Year customer count.[^rass] Reaching the customers in this group who are not already on an incentive list would require the attestation.

[^clf-sc-003]: The Connecticut Light and Power Company d/b/a Eversource Energy, response to CLF-SC-003, Docket No. 26-05-10 (filed September 18, 2026), witnesses Edward A. Davis and Kimberly R. Parsons.

[^rass]: NMR Group, *R2202 Residential Appliance Saturation Survey (RASS)*, final report and detailed tables (September 17, 2025), prepared for the Connecticut Energy Efficiency Board, detailed tables, Appendix E, Table 455. [Final report](https://www.energizect.com/sites/default/files/documents/2025-09-17_Final%20Report_R2202_Res_OTH_ESP_NMR.pdf) and [detailed tables](https://www.energizect.com/sites/default/files/documents/2025-09-17_Final%20Report%20Tables_R2202_Res_OTH_ESP_NMR.pdf).

## CIEC-1(c)

> Please provide Mr. Velez's estimate of the number of customers who would be newly enrolled in Rate HP in each of the first five years after it takes effect, and identify all assumptions used [@ciec_Docket260510First_2026].

**Response.** Between **3,460** and **10,976** customers a year, or **17,300** to **41,552** over five years.

| Year | Floor (customers) | Floor share | Ceiling (customers) | Ceiling share |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2027 | 3,460 | 0.29% | 6,272 | 0.52% |
| 2028 | 3,460 | 0.29% | 7,056 | 0.58% |
| 2029 | 3,460 | 0.29% | 7,840 | 0.65% |
| 2030 | 3,460 | 0.29% | 9,408 | 0.78% |
| 2031 | 3,460 | 0.29% | 10,976 | 0.91% |
| Five-year total | 17,300 | 1.43% | 41,552 | 3.43% |

Assumptions:

- **Timing.** The first five years are 2027 through 2031. The Rate Year begins July 1, 2027 [@clp_Docket260510Exhibit_2026f]. The Company's 2026 installations are counted with existing customers in CIEC-1(b).
- **Enrollment.** Every customer who installs a heat pump enrolls, and none opt out.
- **Floor.** The Company's own forecast of 3,460 residential heat pump installations through its Conservation and Load Management program in 2027, held flat. It excludes installations outside the program.[^clf-sc-001]
- **Ceiling.** ISO New England's forecast of Connecticut residential heat pump additions (8, 9, 10, 12 and 14 thousand housing units in 2027 through 2031),[^isone-2026] multiplied by Eversource's 78.4% share of the households served by Eversource and United Illuminating.[^rass-share]
- **Shares** use the 1,212,521 Rate Year residential customers.

[^clf-sc-001]: The Connecticut Light and Power Company d/b/a Eversource Energy, responses to CLF-SC-001 (including Attachment 1) and CLF-SC-002, Docket No. 26-05-10 (filed September 18, 2026), witness Nina A. Paim.

[^isone-2026]: ISO New England, *Final 2026 Heat Pump Forecast*, "Annual Incremental Increase in HP Stock (1,000 Housing Units)," Connecticut column for residential space heating. [PDF](https://www.iso-ne.com/static-assets/documents/100034/heatfx2026final.pdf).

[^rass-share]: NMR Group, R2202 RASS final report, Table 6, "Sample Size and Achieved Completes": 1,063,376 of 1,356,355 households.
